titles.title: HalfLife1
titles.engine: GoldSrc, WON Half-Life 1.1.0.8 (GOTY tree). hl.exe is the 942,080-byte WON launcher (md5 77cce992..., PE 2001-09-11); it owns the mode list and the mode switch. hw.dll/sw.dll are the engine. Banner 'Half-Life 45/1.1.0.8 (hw build 1792)', network protocol 45.
titles.launch_sets:
1280x960 fullscreen OpenGL on every 1080p LCD, set by the command line.
- All five staged launchers call FLEETRES.BAT and then run `hl.exe -nosierra -full -gl -w %FR_W43% -h %FR_H43% -toconsole [-game bshift|dmc|gearbox|tfc]` (start lines re-read on the share).
- FR_W43/FR_H43 is 1280x960 on .123, .145, .195 and .240 (GAMERES four_three, read at 00:09 and again at about 00:43).
- The launcher's -w/-h override the registry EngineModeW/H (0x413d0d-0x413dbe). It looks for an exact match, then the last same-width fullscreen entry, then index 0 (400x300).
- Measured 1280x960: .123 and .240 (08-31 frames), .246 (now .195) by DISPLAYCFG.
- FLEETRES.EXE md5 bb180f3b... matches the repo. stage-fleetres.py --check reports 213 current; the only failure is Thief2. GAMERES has no HalfLife1 rule.

Correction to the survey's 'latent defect': EngineModeW/H=1920x1080 is not a steady value. The shared HKCU\Software\Valve\Half-Life\Settings key is written three times on every full GAMESYNC, because gs_merge_reg re-merges each title's install.reg on every sync and _priority.txt runs CounterStrike16 3rd and HalfLife1 8th:
1. CounterStrike16/install.reg writes 800x600.
2. The CS16 GAMERES rows write 1920x1080.
3. HalfLife1/install.reg writes ScreenWidth/Height and EngineModeW/H = 1024x768.

So a full sync leaves the key at 1024x768. The 1920x1080 read at 00:09 came from a GAMERES-only pass. None of this changes the launch, because the .bat -w/-h decide it. A bare hl.exe would get 1024x768, or 400x300 while the key holds 1920x1080.
titles.menu_source:
The WON launcher's Configuration > Video 'Video modes' list (CVideoModeDlg, VGUI1). It has two sources:
- The fixed table at file 0xcef70 (400x300 up to 1280x960). These entries are type 0 and shown as '%s windowed' (0x4d06e8).
- IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes, called with flags 0 and callback 0x413a20. The callback keeps a mode only if height/width == 0.75 exactly (double 0.75 at 0x4ae078), height <= 1024, width >= 400, and bpp is 15/16 (the default [0x4e1f30]=16; the launchers pass no -24bpp/-32bpp).

The mode count 0x4ea8c8 is only appended by 0x413b90 and that callback; 0x46b7ae only resets it. So a 16:9 mode can never enter the list.

Runtime check: a read-only probe replayed this filter over each box's own DirectDraw list:
- .123/.145: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960
- .195: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x960
- .240: 400x300, 512x384, 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960

This is identical to the survey.
titles.evidence:
Survey files in /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/goldsrc-halo/ were re-checked:
- won_hl1108_mode_list.asm.txt: the table and the 0.75 constant were re-read from the staged hl.exe with pefile.
- goldsrc_registry_value_matrix.txt: re-run case-insensitively, ASCII and UTF-16. WON hl.exe carries EngineMode*/EngineType/EngineGLDriver/LauncherWidth and no ScreenWidth.

This review, in /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/goldsrc-halo-review/:
- probe_123.txt, probe_145.txt, probe_195.txt, probe_240.txt: the won16 lines, from a read-only DirectDraw/D3D9 probe (source h1080probe.c; uploaded, run and deleted on each box, and the deletion was verified by DIRLIST).
- goldsrc_shared_key_order.txt: _priority.txt positions, the gamesync.c merge-then-gameres order, both install.reg value sets, and the lookup disassembly at 0x413dc0.

Other checks:
- WON 1.1.1.0 patch: hl.exe re-inflated from Files/Game Updates/halflife-1.1.1.0-english.exe at offset 619294 (md5 9ec1de95..., PE 2002-06-06; Files/hl1110.exe is the same file). It has the same 'fcomp 0.75' at 0x13ece and 'cmp esi,0x400' at 0x13ee3; its table adds only 1600x1200.
- compat DB: .123/.240 verified 1280x960; .246 runs 1280x960.
titles.fix:
No configuration change can put 1920x1080 in this menu (confirmed).
- The 0.75 / height<=1024 filter is compiled into WON hl.exe 1.1.0.8, and the 1.1.1.0 patch has the same filter.
- A case-insensitive search of the Windows XP, Installed, Freeware, Mods & Patches, Game Updates, Patches and Inbox trees found no other hw.dll, hl.exe or Xash build. Archives were not opened.
- Keep 1280x960 4:3.

The only real route is to re-stage the HL, TFC and DMC content onto the build-4554 engine already in CounterStrike16, done in the build VM. That tree's valve\ has the Steam-era game/client DLLs and wads but no pak0.pak and no maps (its readme: 'Half-Life maps are totally removed'). HalfLife1\valve\pak0.pak (302,907,835 B) and xeno.wad carry the content. HLDM at 1080p already exists through CounterStrike16\Play Half-Life Deathmatch.bat. Do not hex-patch hl.exe.

Cleanup for the later phase (added by this review):
1. Delete ScreenWidth, ScreenHeight, EngineModeW and EngineModeH from HalfLife1/install.reg, and the same four from CounterStrike16/install.reg. They are per-box values in a byte-identical staged file, they re-pin the shared key on every sync after the CS16 GAMERES pass, and neither GoldSrc launcher needs them. Keep Key, EngineGLDriver, EngineType, *BPP and *Windowed.
2. Fix the HalfLife1 recipe in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py. It still turns '-full -gl -w 1024 -h 768' into '-w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%' and has no FR_W->FR_W43 fix entry, so a regenerated launcher would bring back 400x300.
3. Drop %W%/%H% for EngineModeW/H from the CS16 GAMERES rows (see CounterStrike16).
titles.fix_source: The 4:3 answer is already in the tree. For a re-stage, the build-4554 engine is on the share at Games-Library/CounterStrike16, and the HL content is at Games-Library/HalfLife1/valve (pak0.pak, xeno.wad) and on the retail ISOs under Files/Games/Windows XP/Half-Life GOTY + Opposing Force + Blue Shift/. install.reg and the stager are edits to the library and the repo. Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk:
- Keeping 4:3: none.
- install.reg trim: low, because every launcher passes -w/-h. To verify: run two consecutive full GAMESYNCs on a 1080p box and expect 'gameres: ... 0 value(s) changed' on the second, then relaunch Half-Life.bat and see 1280x960 in DISPLAYCFG get.
- Re-stage onto 4554: high. Protocol goes 45->48, which splits LAN from boxes still on the WON tree until all move. WON-era tfc/dmc client DLLs, Opposing Force, Blue Shift and savegames are unverified, and a new two-box LAN proof is needed.
- Hex patch: high, not recommended.
titles.hw_check:
On an XP LCD box (.145 or .123), where GDI captured fullscreen GoldSrc on 08-31:
1. `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\HalfLife1" "Half-Life.bat"`.
2. `DISPLAYCFG get` should show live 1280x960.
3. `UIKEY ESCAPE` opens the WON shell, which runs at LauncherWidth x LauncherHeight (640x480 on .123/.145/.240, 1280x960 on .195).
4. Configuration > Video > Video modes, then SCREENSHOT 0. The fullscreen entries should end at 1280x960, the 'windowed' entries also end at 1280x960, and there should be no 1920x1080.
5. `taskkill /f /im "hl.exe"` and confirm the desktop is back at 1920x1080x32.

UICLICK on the VGUI1 shell is unverified.

Not run in this review: all four LCD boxes were busy with concurrent sessions (Quake 3 fullscreen on .145, ioquake3 on .195, UIKEY/EXEC traffic on .123 and .240 at 00:37-00:42), so no game was launched.
titles.verifier_notes:
Confirmed:
- menu 'no'
- the per-box 16-bpp lists, now runtime-checked on all four boxes
- the 1.1.1.0 patch claim, re-inflated and re-checked
- the launcher lines
- the stager drift
- the registry-reader matrix

Changed:
- The 'EngineModeW/H=1920x1080 is the live value' framing. A full GAMESYNC ends with HalfLife1/install.reg's 1024x768 in the shared key, because CS16 runs before HL1 in _priority.txt and install.reg is re-merged on every sync. The 1920x1080 seen at 00:09 came from a GAMERES-only pass.
- The fix now also removes the per-box resolution values from both GoldSrc install.reg files.

Side observation, unverified and not affecting resolution: the -w/-h lookup matches entry bpp against registry EngineModeBPP=32 while entries were enumerated at 16, so it takes the same-width fallback (still 1280x960). Whether HL then renders at 16-bit colour was not traced.

The review probe left nothing on any box: the DIRLIST after DELETE showed h1080p.exe absent on all four.

titles.title: CounterStrike16
titles.engine: GoldSrc Steam-era build 4554: Counter-Strike 1.6 No-Steam V42 by ZCP (2009) with RevEmu 9.80. hw.dll is 1,840,440 B (md5 4903e8e8..., PE 2009-06-15); valve/cl_dlls/gameui.dll is dated 2009-04-27. cstrike/cl_dlls has only client.dll, and there is no cstrike optionssubvideo.res, so valve's GameUI and .res are the ones used. Network protocol 48.
titles.launch_sets:
1920x1080 fullscreen OpenGL on every 1080p LCD, set by the command line.
- 'Play Counter-Strike.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT and then runs `hl.exe -game cstrike -full -gl -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%`. FR_W/FR_H is 1920x1080 on all four boxes.
- In CVideoMode_Common::Init (0x1dc6860), -width/-w/-height/-h override the registry ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight. The strings were re-read at 0x1e8ca38/40/44/4c.
- 1920x1080 is in the engine's accepted list on every box (runtime probe), so the exact mode is chosen.
- Measured 1920x1080: .123 (08-31 main menu, and in-game on the fleet server) and .240. On .246 (now .195) the game runs, but the frame is black in capture.
- The 08-31 measurements predate GAMERES (commit 7a26589, 2026-09-04). The install.reg comments ('CS ignores -w/-h') are contradicted by the binary.
- The shared registry key does not decide this launch. Per code (sync order), it is flipped 800x600 -> 1920x1080 -> 1024x768 on every full sync (see HalfLife1).
- Caveat: .240 had no EDID after its ~23:40 reboot (per the brief). If that recurs, FLEETRES falls back to 4:3 answers on that box.
titles.menu_source:
Driver-enumerated, then filtered, in two layers.

Engine layer:
- EnumDisplayModes is called at 0x1dc7ee0 with dwFlags=0, so there is one callback per (w,h,bpp) and no refresh duplicates.
- The callback at 0x1dc7f10 keeps 16:9, 4:3, 5:4 and 16:10 modes with height >= 480 at the configured bpp. ScreenBPP is 32 on all four boxes.
- AddMode stops at 32 entries.

GameUI layer:
- Options > Video, PrepareResolutionList (0x1003ded0), lists 16:9 and 16:10 modes as '%i x %i' only when Aspect Ratio is 'Widescreen'.
- The constructor preselects Widescreen when the current mode is 16:9 or 16:10.

Runtime: the probe replayed the engine filter over each box's own DirectDraw 32-bpp list. Every list contains 1920x1080, and none is near the 32 cap:
- .123: 11 modes
- .145: 12 modes, including 1600x900
- .195: 14 modes, including 1152x648, 1400x1050 and 1600x900
- .240: 11 modes

This matches the survey. The menu itself was not seen on screen in this review.

titles.fix:
None needed for the menu or the launch.

Cleanup for the later phase (the survey's items, confirmed, plus additions from this review):
1. agent/shared/gameres.h CounterStrike16 rows: keep only ScreenWidth=%W%, ScreenHeight=%H%, ScreenBPP=32 and ScreenWindowed=0, which are the values build 4554 reads. EngineModeW/H/BPP/Windowed, EngineType and EngineGLDriver are read only by WON hl.exe, and EngineModeW/H=1920x1080 is a mode that launcher cannot use.
2. Delete ScreenWidth, ScreenHeight, EngineModeW and EngineModeH from both CounterStrike16/install.reg and HalfLife1/install.reg. Both files are re-merged on every sync: CS16's (800x600) right before its own GAMERES rows, and HL1's (1024x768) after them. So every full sync on a 1080p box reports at least 4 changed values and ends with the key at 1024x768. The 'settled box reports 0 value(s) changed' signal can never hold, and the GAMERES rows are overwritten within the same sync.
3. Correct the false comments: gameres.h 'Counter-Strike ... CANNOT override this from its command line'; gameres.h 'ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight are the WON LAUNCHER's values and EngineModeW/H the ENGINE's', which is backwards (EngineMode* belong to WON hl.exe, Screen* to the 4554 engine); and the 'ignores -w/-h' text in both install.reg files.
4. Update tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py (around line 150, which requires EngineModeW/H = %W%/%H%) and tests/native/test_gameres.c t_goldsrc_reaches_the_panel (CHECK_EQ engw/engh 1920/1080). Both currently pin the defect.
titles.fix_source: Repo edits: agent/shared/gameres.h and the two tests. Library edits: CounterStrike16/install.reg and HalfLife1/install.reg, through the staged-game fix loop (purge, GAMESYNC, push to the fleet). The install.reg edits change file size, so the smbclient mtime caveat does not apply. Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk: None for gameplay: every GoldSrc launcher passes -w/-h, and build 4554 honours them (disassembly, plus the 08-31 1920x1080 result taken while install.reg still pinned 4:3 values). No effect on the fleet HLDS, the a2s proxies or BCShield, because resolution is client-local. To verify: two consecutive full GAMESYNCs should show 0 values changed on the second; CS should come up at 1920x1080 and HL1 at 1280x960 through their .bat launchers.
titles.hw_check:
On .145 or .123 (XP, where GDI captures GoldSrc fullscreen):
1. `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\CounterStrike16" "Play Counter-Strike.bat"`.
2. SCREENSHOT 0 should show the VGUI2 main menu at 1920x1080.
3. UICLICK 'Options' (about 62,974 at 1920x1080), open the Video tab, and SCREENSHOT. Expect Aspect Ratio 'Widescreen' and Resolution '1920 x 1080'.
4. Open the Resolution combo and SCREENSHOT the dropdown.
5. Press Cancel or Escape, not OK, so no setting is written.
6. `taskkill /f /im "hl.exe"`.

Synthetic UIKEY is proven fullscreen on this build (.123, 08-31). UICLICK on VGUI2 is not yet proven.

On .195 (Win7) the frame captures black: prove the mode with DISPLAYCFG get plus WINLIST, and view the list in a -window relaunch.

Not run in this review: all four LCD boxes were busy with concurrent Quake 3 and other sessions.

titles.title: Halo
titles.engine: Halo: Combat Evolved PC, Gearbox D3D9 port, version 1.10 (halo.exe 2,822,144 B, md5 b7aa8f68..., FileVersion 01.00.10.0621, PE 2014-05-13), from Bungie's signed 1.0.10 patch. d3d9 is loaded dynamically; config.txt is the card database.
titles.launch_sets:
1920x1080 at 60 Hz fullscreen, set by the command line.
- 'Play Halo.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT and then runs `halo.exe %HALO_NOVIDEO% -vidmode %FR_W%,%FR_H%,%FR_HZ%`, which is `-vidmode 1920,1080,60` on all four LCD boxes (persisted desktop rate 60).
- The -vidmode parser at 0x5168c0 ('%d,%d,%d', defaults 800x600@60) bypasses the menu list.
- HALO_NOVIDEO is set only where the vcrmp service runs, i.e. .124's vcr-kmd.
- Measured: .240 and .246 (now .195) verified at 1920x1080@60 on 08-31 (real frames: 240_Halo_Play_Halo.png, and 246_Halo_Play_Halo.png is non-black even on Win7). .123 runs at that mode, but the capture there was black.
- The 1080 Keystone overlay files (1080log.ksml, 1080editbox.ksml, gallery/editbox1080.png) are staged.
- The FLEETRES payload and the stager check are current. There is no GAMERES rule for Halo, by design.
titles.menu_source:
Driver-enumerated with filters. Settings > Video Setup rebuilds its list when opened (0x4baf20 -> 0x4bad40 -> 0x4baba0). It enumerates D3D9 X8R8G8B8 modes from the highest index down and keeps a mode only if all of these hold:
- 640 <= w <= 4800 and 480 <= h <= 3600, refresh <= 120
- not 720x480, 720x576, 848x480 or 848x576
- w <= MaximumResolution (default 0x1000 at 0x69fe3c; the staged config.txt sets it for no card, checked with grep -n -i)
- the video-memory width cap: <=32 MB -> w<=1024, <=64 MB -> w<=1280, <=128 MB -> w<=1600, above that no cap
- in windowed mode only, w and h below the desktop size

AddMode keeps at most 32 resolutions with up to 8 refresh rates each.

Corrected detail: the video-memory cap runs when MaximumResolution is at its default OR -vidmode is on the command line, and the launcher passes -vidmode.

Where the video-memory figure comes from, now traced: 0x722bb0 is Halo's own DirectDraw measurement (0x57dae3-0x57dc44). It is the minimum of the GetAvailableVidMem totals for caps 0x4200, 0x10007000, 0x10005000 and 0x10004040, rounded up to 64 MB steps, taken for the device that matches D3D9's DeviceName (0x57d479/0x57d4ac). Only a config.txt 'UMA' card replaces it, with a RAM-derived 8-64 MB value (handler 0x57d250). In config.txt, UMA appears only under Intel's Unknown entry.

Runtime: the same measurement run on each box gives .123 576 MB, .145 512 MB, .195 512 MB and .240 320 MB, all above 128 MB. Halo's full filter over each box's D3D9 list keeps 1920x1080@60 (and also @50/@59 on .195).

- probe_123.txt, probe_145.txt, probe_195.txt, probe_240.txt: the halo_value and halo1_list lines.

Other evidence:
- probe2_halo2_dirs.json (survey): ExitFlag 'bad 1' on .123, 'bad 2' on .145/.240, 'clean' on .195; Halo 'Unknown' card memo keys on .145/.240.
- Staged files read: Play Halo.bat, config.txt (md5 4e33300c..., edited 2026-09-28 13:35; no card sets MaximumResolution or UMA except Intel's Unknown), NOTES-halo.txt.
- Frames: /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/perbox/evidence/240_Halo_Play_Halo.png and 246_Halo_Play_Halo.png.
titles.hw_check:
This needs a person at the keyboard: Halo's shell ignores the agent's synthetic keys and absolute clicks (NOTES-halo.txt; the .240 windowed frames from 09-01).
1. On .145 or .123, launch 'Play Halo.bat' fullscreen. Do not add -window, because windowed mode drops every mode at or above the desktop size.
2. At the 'did not exit correctly' dialog (ExitFlag bad on .123/.145/.240), choose Continue Anyway, not Safe Mode.
3. Settings > Video Setup > Resolution, and step through to 1920 x 1080.

On the agent side: SCREENSHOT 0, and `DISPLAYCFG get` should read live 1920x1080 during the run. On .195 (Win7), GDI did capture Halo fullscreen on 08-31, so SCREENSHOT 0 can record the person's menu there as well.

If the list tops out at 1024, 1280 or 1600 wide, the video-memory cap fired, which contradicts the measured 320-576 MB.

Not run in this review: the boxes were busy.
titles.verifier_notes:
Confirmed:
- menu 'yes'
- launch at 1920x1080@60
- the filter chain as described

Strengthened: the survey could not find the writer of 0x722bb0 and inferred it from the cards' real memory. It is Halo's own DirectDraw local-video-memory measurement, and replaying it on each box gives 576/512/512/320 MB, well above the 128 MB threshold. With Halo's exact filters over each box's live D3D9 list, 1920x1080 survives everywhere.

Corrected: the cap branch also triggers on -vidmode, not only on the default MaximumResolution. The outcome is the same.

The menu itself is still unobserved, because the shell cannot be driven by the agent.

titles.title: Halo2
titles.engine: Halo 2 for Windows Vista 1.00.00.11081 (halo2.exe 14,677,368 B, md5 8430e098..., PE 2007-04-30, SubsystemVersion 4.0). It uses D3D9 (Direct3DCreate9Ex where present), GFWL (xlive.dll) and d3dx9_31. On XP it runs through Loader.exe plus the dwmapi/mf/MFPlat/XTaskDlg/Wow shims.
titles.launch_sets:
No per-box mode. Nothing in the tree sets one: 'Play Halo 2.bat' has no FLEETRES, there is no GAMERES rule, install.reg holds only GameInstallDir, and halo2.exe has no resolution switch (confirmed switches: -windowed, -novsync, -nosound, -monitor:, -highquality, -mce, -svu, -hrd).

On first run the game creates HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings from a compiled block: 1024x768@60, or the low-spec block of 800x600 (0x864e2c).

Live values:
- .123 and .145 (XP): 800x600 with AA 0 and LOD 2 (the low-spec block).
- .195 (Win7): 1024x768 (verified running on 09-01; the frames are real 1024x768 GDI captures of the fullscreen surface).
- .240: no key. It holds the full tree, and its agent log lists a 'Halo 2.lnk', but the capability gate now refuses it for disk space (C: 765 MB free per HWPROFILE) and it has never run there.

Validation at 0x663597 picks the largest listed mode no larger than ScreenResX x ScreenResY with refresh <= ScreenRefresh+1.
titles.menu_source:
A hardcoded whitelist intersected with the driver. The 10-entry whitelist is at 0x865010. In fullscreen, 0x662bfb calls EnumAdapterModes at the desktop format and keeps only whitelist entries, with up to 8 refresh rates each. Windowed shows all 10 with no driver check.

Confirmed by this review:
- AspectRatio (0xe3a7cc) is written only by its setter 0x66303b and read nowhere.
- The whitelist's aspect column is read only by 0x662fa3, which reports the current mode's aspect.
- The c_resolution_edit_list constructor (around 0x64f93c) sizes itself with 0x662f1e() and formats every entry with L"%dx%d". There is no aspect filter.

Runtime (probe, D3D9 X8R8G8B8 intersected with the whitelist):
- .123/.145/.195: 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x720, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1680x1050, 1920x1080
- .240: the same without 1680x1050

Caveat: the menu is reachable only where the game renders, which today means .195 (Win7). On XP, .123 was measured failed on 09-01 (the window never paints and exits on the first key). .145 has no sign of ever reaching a menu: no Halo 2 data folder, an empty C:\h2.log, and leftover 09-01 _dbg.bat/_go.bat.

This review, in /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/goldsrc-halo-review/:
- halo2_menu_aspect_and_key.asm.txt: all references to 0xe3a7cc; the 0x662fa3 aspect-column reader; the menu constructor's use of the count accessor; the L"%dx%d" format; gameres.c gr_w_reg using RegCreateKeyExA.

titles.fix:
Write the per-box mode into HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings before launch: ScreenResX=%FR_W%, ScreenResY=%FR_H%, ScreenRefresh=%FR_HZ%, DisplayMode=0.
- In the launcher: add Halo2 to scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py (stage FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT, call FLEETRES.BAT, then guarded `FLEETRES.EXE -reg HKCU ... dword` lines before the dwmapi/Loader branch).
- In the agent: GR_OP_REG rows in agent/shared/gameres.h.

Corrections to the survey's plan:
1. The GAMERES ScreenRefresh row must use %FRHZ% (the twin of FR_HZ), not %HZ%. Otherwise the two writers disagree wherever the best rate at the target differs from the persisted desktop rate.
2. gr_w_reg creates the key with RegCreateKeyExA, so after a sync a box that has never run Halo 2 holds a PARTIAL key. halo2.exe's loader (0x663b3e) copies the whole default block over the settings on any missing value, so the launcher's full 11-value write must be triggered by a value GAMERES does not write (for example `reg query ... /v LevelOfDetail` failing), not by the key being absent.
3. Pick the full-block defaults per OS: XP's own first-run choice was AA 0 / LOD 2.
4. Only .195 benefits today. XP boxes first need the black-window fault fixed, and .240 is gated for disk.
5. Run validate-staged-library.py afterwards; its fleetres check catches a half-staged title.
6. Separately, clean up .145's non-staged leftovers (C:\Games\Halo2\_dbg.bat, _go.bat and C:\h2.log, from a 09-01 session; this review left them in place).

Low. These are per-user DWORDs the game writes itself. Worst case, the validator steps down to the largest listed mode, or switches to windowed if nothing fits.
- A user's in-menu resolution choice is overwritten at the next launch or sync, which is fleet policy.
- Frame rate at 1080p on the HD 5450 (.195) is unmeasured.
- No multiplayer or GFWL effect.
- The FLEETRES lines must not reorder the dwmapi shim / Loader logic.
- The GAMERES rows need matching entries in tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py.
titles.hw_check:
Use .195 (Win7): it is the only box where Halo 2 renders, and GDI captured its fullscreen menu there on 09-01. Do not use .145 or .123.
1. After the change, read the values back with `REGREAD HKCU Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings` (all 11 DWORDs present).
2. Launch 'Play Halo 2.bat'. `DISPLAYCFG get` should show live 1920x1080 and WINLIST should show 'Halo 2' at 0,0-1920x1080. SCREENSHOT 0.
3. Main menu > SETTINGS > video > resolution list, viewed in fullscreen (windowed lists all 10 entries without asking the driver). A 'confirm resolution' countdown screen follows any change.

How the 09-01 session drove the Halo 2 menu is not recorded, so whether UIKEY reaches it is unknown. If it does not, a person has to do this once.
